topics.flagship-ru-ua: Ukraine and Russia both reported cyberattacks on emergency alert apps (6 outlets): Ukraine's air raid alert app was hacked and users received false threat alerts, while Russia reported a 'massive cyberattack' on its own emergency app. A single outlet reportedly said Russia launched a ballistic missile at Kyiv after Zelenskyy warned of a major strike, and that the false alerts warned of nuclear and chemical attacks. Evacuees from occupied Oleshky reached Kyiv-controlled territory after a reportedly Melania Trump-brokered localized truce, Kyiv claimed a hit on a Russian rocket fuel plant, and a Russian airstrike destroyed the Kramatorsk city council executive committee building. Putin was quoted as saying a war with Europe would have no winners, and a Sputnik interview with George Galloway criticized UK war-preparation rhetoric.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Iran and the US are exploring diplomacy through mediators (3 outlets). Iran says it could reopen Hormuz in a shorter period if conditions are met, while Trump says the US still has targets to 'take care of' and that talks are 'going fine'. Iran's supreme leader warned of an immediate response to any US or Israeli attack. Single-outlet reports say the US is massing about 20,000 sailors and marines in the Arabian Sea and that Israel has completed preparations for renewed fighting with Iran but has made no decision to resume attacks. Other items: Yemeni government forces seized positions in al-Jawf, and the US called the Turkey-Libya maritime deal 'unhelpful and provocative'.
topics.T15: Bolivia declared an emergency as El Niño intensifies, with at least 78,000 families already affected by drought (single outlet). In India, the Cyclone Arnab death toll in Odisha rose to 6 with 11 missing, and flood-related sanitation and disease fears persist in Asika. Japan launched a disaster management agency with regional hubs, and Panama's archbishop appealed for children affected by an earthquake. The Turkey-Syria earthquake item (17,000 dead) appears to be an old story resurfacing, and the remaining items are minor relief or preparedness pieces.
topics.T01: A Myanmar military airstrike on Karen forces near the border reportedly damaged at least 17 homes and several public buildings across the Salween River in Thailand's Sob Moei district. El Salvador's Bukele denied that Salvadoran forces in Haiti bombed civilians, and Algeria is reportedly sending troops to Niger for the first time in decades. A senior RSF commander in Sudan defected, accusing the group's leadership of nepotism. All are single-outlet reports.
topics.T02: More than 28 million people in the DRC are not getting enough to eat, according to the latest IPC alert, and the number is expected to rise amid conflict, Ebola and climate shocks (2 outlets). Other items cover Sudanese artists preserving culture during the war, the burden on families of fighters killed in Yemen, and ActionAid Nigeria demanding transparency over a proposed ₦50,000 cash support scheme.
topics.T03: Coverage is limited to a single DW explainer on biological weapons, noting concern over biotech and AI developments. It describes no specific incident or attack.
topics.T04: Nigeria's NCDC said six contacts of a confirmed Ebola case were due to exit quarantine after completing 21 days of monitoring without symptoms. A Weld County, Colorado dairy was quarantined after bird flu was found in its milk, the state's first such case since 2024. The other items are an opinion piece on whether Ebola could turn pandemic and an Indian biotech symposium, neither of which reports a new development.
topics.T05: Tensions are high in Poland as Donald Tusk accuses rivals and the head of state of falsifying facts, while he himself is accused of a 'constitutional coup' (2 outlets). London police arrested 48 as hundreds protested the Palestine Action ban days before a UK Supreme Court appeal. Single-outlet items include a report that Marco Rubio publicly urged Cubans to work with the CIA, commentary on US pressure on European governments, and political rallies in India (the INDIA bloc rally and a Manipur peace rally in Imphal).
topics.T06: French authorities expressed relief that cost-of-living protests were less violent than on previous weekends (5 outlets), though a Molotov cocktail attack on police during Halloween riots prompted an attempted-murder investigation in Paris. Rioters looted stores and set fires in Frankfurt, and more than 100,000 students rallied across Germany against spending cuts and plans to revive military conscription. Further action is expected, and coverage links the unrest to cost of living, education and conscription grievances.
topics.T07: A single outlet reports Trump saying Iran's nuclear program has been eliminated, but that one or two sites remain that the US 'can take care of in ten minutes'. This is a rhetorical claim, and nothing else on nuclear issues appears in this topic.
topics.T08: Colombia's new president reportedly claims over 32,000 arrests in ten weeks as it joins Trump's anti-cartel coalition, and Costa Rica jailed more than 120 inmates in a new mega-prison built with Salvadoran help. Nigerian troops rescued 11 kidnap victims and stopped a terrorist ambush in Kebbi (2 outlets). Other items include Indonesian detentions of alleged TPNPB-OPM members in Papua, an Australian political row over a released convicted terrorist, and a Jordan village named City of Culture after an attack. The Moscow terror-plot arrest is covered under T14.
topics.T10: A single outlet reports that China is testing an uncrewed trimaran submarine that could carry 16-18 missiles. South Korea plans 21.3 trillion won for AI and chip projects (4 outlets), nearly double this year's funding, with a higher defense budget. Russia is reportedly nearing completion of a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad that raises NATO concern, and Google is reportedly in early talks to join the Golden Dome missile defense program. Indian Air Force leadership changes and fifth-generation fighter commentary round out the topic.
topics.T11: The US Navy arrived in Chattogram for CARAT-2026 with Bangladesh (2 outlets), and US Pacific Air Forces and the Bangladesh Air Force began a five-day exercise running through 5 November. An India-Australia joint exercise concluded in Keralam. Irish troops in Lebanon face a change of flag as the UN mandate ends and a new EU mission limited to training Lebanese troops begins.
topics.T12: Binance said 90% of losses from a $6.3bn hack are covered and is resuming withdrawals, as the FBI attributed the attack to the North Korea-affiliated group TraderTraitor (5 outlets). Chainalysis disclosed a breach involving 'offensive agentic techniques'. Sophos reported that a ransomware gang used AI agents to move through victim networks. A zero-click Android 'SMS of Death' flaw was reported, and the Pentagon is reportedly asking whether a hack that pushed freezers at French supermarkets to 122 degrees also hit US military commissaries.
topics.T13: Coverage is thin: a UK report says more than 200 unaccompanied migrant children arrive by boat in Dover every month, and the US Deputy Secretary of State said the quick failure of migrant caravans shows the power of cartels over migration. Both are single-outlet pieces with no major new event.
topics.T14: Russian police arrested a minor over an alleged plot to attack Moscow after a US tip-off, Russian news agencies reported (6 outlets). The US Embassy in Moscow had issued a rare, specific warning of a 'credible threat' of an attack causing mass casualties at a popular park in the capital. A pointer notes Sen. Chris Murphy said he was briefed on a US plan for potential renewed strikes on Iran.
topics.T16: US midterms are on Tuesday, with 35 Senate seats and all 435 House seats up and Republicans holding a 53-47 Senate majority. The Trump DOJ has reportedly sued Alaska over certification if the Republican incumbent loses, Trump announced over $15 billion in farm aid, and Democrats are split over support for Israel. Bulgaria's acting President Iliana Yotova won the presidential runoff decisively, and one outlet says Trump lost allies in elections in Serbia and Brazil.

bluf: Russia arrested a minor over an alleged plot to attack Moscow after a US tip-off, and the US Embassy in Moscow had issued a rare, specific warning of a 'credible threat' of a mass-casualty attack at a popular park (6 outlets). The FBI attributed the $6.3bn Binance hack to the North Korea-affiliated group TraderTraitor; Binance says 90% of losses are covered and is resuming withdrawals. French cost-of-living protest violence eased, but riots and looting hit Frankfurt and more than 100,000 German students rallied against cuts and conscription, with more action expected. Iran and the US are exploring diplomacy through mediators, and Iran says it could reopen Hormuz faster if conditions are met, but Trump says the US still has targets to 'take care of' and Iran's supreme leader threatened an immediate response to any attack. In Poland, Tusk is accused of a 'constitutional coup' while he accuses rivals and the head of state of falsifying facts and undermining the rule of law. Separately, Ukraine and Russia both reported cyberattacks on emergency alert apps that sent false threat alerts, and one outlet reportedly said the alerts warned of nuclear and chemical attacks. The same outlet reportedly said Russia fired a ballistic missile at Kyiv. Single-outlet reports also say the US is massing about 20,000 sailors and marines in the Arabian Sea and that Israel has completed preparations for renewed fighting with Iran, with no decision made.
